data.title: Pick the route
data.ask: Approve the strategy and one route. Nothing downstream is built until you do.
open_questions: Is this paid social (vertical, sound off first) aimed at product-page visits, or a different placement or goal? (A04, A06)
Does 'one cup at a time' mean the dripper brews one cup, or that each dripper is glazed one at a time? (A02)
Can we cast three kids, or should one child carry all three mornings? (A07)
OK to show the $38 price on the end frame? (A10)

strategy.proposition: Their news keeps, one cup at a time.
strategy.tension: Who: parents who make coffee on a machine at home before school drop-off. The moment is mid-breakfast, while each kid brings them something that needs an answer before they leave. This is the recommended primary buyer. It narrows A05, and the choice goes to Lucas (see blockers). Proxy media can buy (assumption): paid social audiences of parents of school-age children with an interest in home coffee or coffee machines. In their voice: I want to hear their news the second it happens, yet I want one stretch of the morning when nobody needs me, and I'd hate to admit I'd rather they waited. [H1] What they'd hate to admit is that wanting those minutes makes them a less present parent. The cost isn't time. Take the product away and the conflict is still there: the tension never mentions coffee.

routes.central_idea: News that can't wait can, for one cup, and it's still news when the dripper lifts.
routes.emotional_promise: The small relief of news surviving the wait: a fist that loosens once to check and clenches again opens on a tooth at the lift.
routes.product_role: Job: the viewer's clock. The viewer reads the dripper. Drops fall from it into a clear glass against the dark cabinet and count down the wait, and the lift ends it. The viewer sees the cup; the child beyond the island watches only the dripper. First appearance: 0 s, draining at 20-50% of frame height, frame right (the vertical rule is by 3 s). Brand assets: the dripper's shape and glaze, taken from the physical sample (none supplied yet); the lift as the full stop; A10 text over S03, on the end frame only. A rival cone would run the same clock, so the brand rests on A10's words landing after one child and one cup. Guard: no scale timer, wall clock or steam close-up (these imply brew time or heat). The parent reacts to the news, never to the coffee (taste). Proof: "Solace makes a ceramic pour-over dripper that costs $38." "The dripper is glazed by hand, one cup at a time."
routes.execution_example:
D01 'Tooth', 30 s, 9:16, 24 fps. Keeps: the premise and story seed as written, with a clear glass in place of the mug so the drops read (question for Lucas). The parent shows as hands and forearms. The child is cut at the shoulders until the insert. Look: locked-off 28mm above dripper height, angled down across the island; dripper, glass, tape and toes inside 20-60% of frame; east window camera left, 5000K, 3:1; scene sound only; one cut, on the lift. Tags: every P beat assumes A11's shoot (no budget authorized; the C fallback is in assumptions).
0-2 s [P]: the parent's hand sets the kettle down at the frame's right edge, on the parent's side (click). The stream from the dripper into the clear glass breaks into drops. Beyond the island, small socked toes slide onto the new tape over the worn gray strip and stop. The parent's near hand stops halfway to the glass, then settles flat beside it.
2-19 s [P, risky: liquid; fallback: A03, with the drips on sound and the lift as the only cue]: the frame holds. The drops slow and the level in the glass stops rising. 9-12 s is the beat only this route has: the fist loosens one knuckle, checks, and clenches again. Nobody else moves.
19-21 s [P, risky: a hand working the dripper; fallback: a hand double on a locked take]: the last drop, a beat, then the parent lifts the dripper off the glass and sets it on the oak (ceramic on wood).
21-24.5 s [P, 50mm insert; the cut on the lift]: the fist opens on a tooth.
24.5-27.5 s [P]: glass in one hand, the parent holds out the other palm. The tooth drops in and a thumb turns it over once.
27.5-30 s [P+C; fallback R+C once a render exists]: cut to the S03 end frame: the dripper where it was set down, no glass under it; A10 text.
Shortest cut (8 s): 0-1.5 s toes land on the tape as drops fall into the glass; 1.5-2.5 s the fist loosens a knuckle and clenches again; 2.5-3.5 s the last drop and the lift; 3.5-4.5 s the fist opens on the tooth; 4.5-6 s the dripper where it was set down, no text; 6-8 s A10 text.
CTA: the platform link button to the Solace dripper product page. No CTA text on screen beyond A10.
Recurring device: the held two-shot, one check on the news mid-hold, and the cut on the lift. D02: the slip and pen are held at arm's length. Mid-hold the slip dips an inch, the pen taps the dotted line, and both come back up. The parent signs against the fridge without setting the glass down. D03: mid-hold, two fingers lift off the forehead and press flat again. On the insert the hand comes down on home-cut bangs (face shown on purpose; A15 fallback). Back in the two-shot, the glass rises out of the top of frame for a long first sip and stays up.

routes.central_idea: The quiet isn't taken from the kids; they're the ones who keep it, one cup at a time.
routes.emotional_promise: The guilt easing as your kid keeps the rule for you: a sock toe pressing the tape's lifting corner flat, then waiting.
routes.product_role: Job: the child's signal. The child reads the dripper. From the tape, the island's edge hides the mug, so the dripper's outline standing above the edge means wait and its outline lifting away means go. The route needs no visible last drop, so it still works if A03 or A17 fails. First appearance: 0 s, in outline above the island's edge at 25-40% of frame height. Brand assets: the dripper's outline against the dark cabinet (taken from the sample); the lift as the full stop; A10 text over S03 on the end frame, which is the route's only close product shot. A rival cone gives the same signal, so the outline and A10 carry the brand. Guard: no timer or clock in frame. The parent reacts to the news, never to the coffee. Proof: "Solace makes a ceramic pour-over dripper that costs $38." "The dripper is glazed by hand, one cup at a time."
routes.execution_example:
D01 'Tooth', 30 s, 9:16, 24 fps. Keeps: the tape, the toes, the fist that opens on a tooth, the lift, one cup, and the premise's 'the child sees the dripper, never the cup'. Drops: the viewer seeing the last drops fall (question for Lucas). Look: locked-off 50mm at the child's hip height, from behind them; feet and tape at 55-62% of frame, dripper at 25-40%; window beyond the island, 5000K, 4:1; sound from the child's position; no cut until the end frame. Tags: every P beat assumes A11's shoot.
0-1.5 s [P]: the child walks in past the lens, back to us, frame left. Across the room the parent sets the kettle down (a small click). Beyond the island's edge the dripper stands draining, the mug hidden.
1.5-2 s [P]: socked feet stop on the new tape over the worn gray strip.
2-6 s [P] is the beat only this route has: a corner of the new tape has lifted. A sock toe presses it flat, presses again, then settles back behind the line.
6-19 s [P, risky: the dripper's legibility at phone size; fallback: move the island edge nearer, with the dripper up to 40% of frame height]: the frame holds. The fist sits at the child's side. Beyond, the parent doesn't move. The drip is heard, small and far.
19-21 s [P, risky: a hand working the dripper; fallback: a hand double on a locked take]: the parent's hand lifts the dripper, and its outline leaves the island's edge. It is set down (ceramic on wood, far off).
21-25 s [P]: the fist comes up and opens. The child holds the tooth up between finger and thumb, white against the dark cabinet, with the parent soft beyond.
25-27.5 s [P]: the parent raises the mug an inch toward the tooth. Nobody speaks.
27.5-30 s [P+C; fallback R+C]: the one cut, to the S03 end frame: the dripper where it was set down; A10 text.
Shortest cut (8 s): 0-1.5 s the child walks in and stops on the tape, dripper beyond; 1.5-2.5 s the toe presses the lifting corner flat; 2.5-4 s the dripper lifts away; 4-5 s the tooth held up; 5-6.5 s the dripper where it was set down, no text; 6.5-8 s A10 text.
CTA: the platform link button to the Solace dripper product page.
Recurring device: the same frame from behind the child. Each child tends the line once, and only the child and the news change. D02: the eldest slides a sock back behind the line and holds out the slip and pen. After the lift the parent signs against the fridge, mug in hand. D03: the middle child smooths the tape with a heel. The hand comes down and the child turns to profile on a ragged edge of bangs (face shown on purpose; A15 fallback). The parent takes a long first sip, face neutral.

routes.central_idea: Answering mid-pour gets them a glance; finishing the cup gets them your eyes.
routes.emotional_promise: The pleasure of giving your whole attention at once: eyes up from the lifted dripper to a small fist dropping a tooth into your palm.
routes.product_role: Job: the parent's eye line. The parent reads the dripper: one glance at the child, then eyes down to the cone until the lift, then eyes up to a frame with no dripper in it. For a machine user it puts the dripper on their own counter, at their own eye level. First appearance: 0 s, draining at the bottom of the safe band in the glance, then at frame center for the hold. The glance frame doubles as each episode's S02 cover, with the news and the cone in one frame. Brand assets: the cone's rim and glaze seen from above for about 18 s (taken from the sample); the lift as the only thing that frees the frame; A10 text over S03 on the end frame. Rival gate: the hold is built on one visible feature of the physical dripper that shows it was glazed by hand (F2). It has to sit on the rim or flange, the part the filter doesn't cover, such as where the glaze stops, and it has to read from above at phone size. It is shown, never called one of a kind. If the sample has no such feature, the brand rests on A10's words alone, and the hold carries only the idea (where your eyes are). Guard: no scale readout, timer or steam macro (these imply brew time or heat). The D03 sip is a pause, not a verdict on taste. Proof: "Solace makes a ceramic pour-over dripper that costs $38." "The dripper is glazed by hand, one cup at a time."
routes.execution_example:
D01 'Tooth', 30 s, 9:16, 24 fps. Keeps: the kettle going down, the toes on the re-laid tape by 2 s, the parent clocking the child and then watching the dripper, the fist, the lift, one cup, the tooth. Drops (questions for Lucas): the visible last drops, which read as the water line from above instead, and the parent's face (A11's on-camera parent becomes hands). Look: parent's-eye POV, locked; a 35mm glance, one cut to a 20mm eyes down on the cone, one tilt up on the lift; pendant over the island, 3500K top-down, 2:1; scene sound at the parent's head. Tags: every P beat assumes A11's shoot.
0-2 s [P, risky: a hand and the kettle; fallback: a hand double on a locked take, product stays live]: the glance. Your hand sets the kettle down on your side of the island (click). The cone drains at the bottom of the safe band. Across the island, small socked toes slide onto the new tape over the worn gray strip, large in the upper half, and stop by 2 s. A clenched fist hangs beside them.
2-20 s [P, the tone's one cut, to the drain; risky: the drawdown at phone size; fallback: A03, with the lift alone as the cue and the drip on sound]: eyes down. The water line sits high in the cone, then sinks into the bed, and the bed flattens. At the top of the safe band the toes stay put. Your hands rest flat on either side of the mug. You don't look up again.
20-21.5 s [P, risky: a hand working the dripper; fallback: a hand double]: the last drip. Your hand lifts the dripper off the mug and sets it down at frame left (ceramic on oak).
21.5-24 s [P]: eyes up, the frame's only move, from the mug to the child. The child has stepped from the tape to the island's far edge, fist held out on their own side. It is the first frame without the dripper.
24-27.5 s [P]: your palm crosses the island to the child; the child never reaches in. The fist opens over it and a tooth drops in. Your other hand brings the mug up into the bottom of the frame.
27.5-30 s [P+C; fallback R+C]: cut to the S03 end frame: the dripper where you set it down, no mug; A10 text.
Shortest cut (8 s): 0-1.5 s kettle down, cone draining, toes land large on the tape; 1.5-3 s eyes down: the water line sinks, the last drip, the lift; 3-4.5 s eyes up, the fist drops a tooth into your palm; 4.5-6 s the dripper where you set it down, no text; 6-8 s A10 text.
CTA: the platform link button to the Solace dripper product page. No CTA text beyond A10.
Recurring device: one glance, eyes down on the dripper until the lift, then eyes up to a frame with no dripper in it. D02: the glance lands on a slip and an uncapped pen at arm's length. After the lift you take the pen and sign against the fridge, mug in your other hand. D03: the glance lands on a hand pressed flat to a forehead, the first head it reaches. Eyes up to the hand coming down on home-cut bangs (face shown on purpose; A15 fallback). The mug rises into frame for a long first sip, with the bangs over the rim.

data.recommendation:
'Their news keeps, one cup at a time' plays at 20-27.5 s: eyes come up only after the lift, and the tooth still lands in your palm as news. The 0-2 s glance puts the child's toes on the re-laid tape in frame before the cone can pass for a pour-over routine video, which machine users scroll past as gear for quiet mornings (H4). Success: the muted pre-flight gate, where 6 of 8 parents name the coffee as what the child waits for. The full 30 s D01 serves it, because the glance shows the parent has seen the child before the hold.
Gives up: the premise's 'we see the last drops fall'. R3 reads the drawdown as a water line from above, where R1 shows drops falling into a clear glass. It also splits parent and child across a cut where R1 holds them in one frame, and it never shows the parent's face.
Failure: 2-20 s. At phone size the drawdown seen from above can look like a still brown circle, and the toes at 20-30% of frame shrink to a strip of sock. Fix: cut to the cone while the water is still high, so the sinking line visibly travels, and keep white socks against the tape. The glance has already shown the toes large, so in the hold they only need to stay present. Never move the tape toward the kettle to make it bigger.
Kill test: in the muted pre-flight gate, parents read the POV as a parent ignoring a child: fewer than 6 of 8 name the coffee as what the child waits for, or they describe the wait as neglect even after the glance. Then first person has turned the guilt onto the viewer instead of dissolving it. Switch to R1, where both are in one frame and the rule reads as the family's, not yours.
Case R1: A12's phone test (A03). If the drops in R1's clear glass read muted at phone size and R3's water line from above doesn't, R1 is the pick.
Case R2: proof point 3 / A03 and A17 (Blocked). If A12's phone test shows the drawdown doesn't read from any angle, R2 is the pick, because its cue is the dripper leaving the cup as seen from the tape.
